query: My tokio server shares a HashMap between connection tasks. I switched from std::sync::Mutex to tokio::sync::Mutex because tokio::spawn complained that the future cannot be sent between threads safely, even though I call drop(guard) before the .await. Is that the right fix?
expected_behavior: Explains that std::sync::MutexGuard is not Send and that drop(guard) does not help because the compiler computes Send from scopes, so the guard must end in a block scope before the .await
Recommends keeping std::sync::Mutex for plain data that is never locked across .await, for example by locking inside a non-async method of a wrapper struct
States that tokio::sync::Mutex is for guards held across .await (such as I/O resources) and usually does not improve performance
Mentions sharding or a task owning the state as the fix for real contention
Cites https://tokio.rs/tokio/tutorial/shared-state

query: Review this loop: loop { tokio::select! { _ = socket.read_exact(&mut header) => handle(&header), _ = tx.send(event) => {}, _ = tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(30)) => break } }. Sometimes messages vanish and the 30 second timeout never fires.
expected_behavior: Identifies read_exact as not cancel safe, so partial header bytes are lost when another branch wins
Identifies mpsc::Sender::send in a losing branch as dropping the message, and recommends reserve() then Permit::send
Explains that the sleep is recreated on every iteration, and recommends creating it once outside the loop, pinning it with tokio::pin! and selecting on &mut sleep
Suggests merging the sources into one stream or moving the non-cancel-safe read out of select!
Cites https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/macro.select.html

query: I built a runtime with tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread().build() for a sync library wrapper and call rt.block_on(tokio::time::sleep(d)) and TcpStream::connect through it. It panics. Also, tasks I spawn on it never progress between calls. What is wrong?
expected_behavior: Explains that a Builder runtime has no I/O or time driver and must call enable_all()
Explains that sleep(d) passed directly to block_on is created outside the runtime and should be wrapped in an async block
Explains that a current-thread runtime runs spawned tasks only while Runtime::block_on runs, and suggests a multi-thread runtime or a runtime on its own thread fed by mpsc for background work
Cites https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/runtime/index.html and https://tokio.rs/tokio/topics/bridging

query: Write a Windows named pipe server with tokio that accepts many clients concurrently, plus a client that connects to it reliably.
expected_behavior: Creates the first instance with ServerOptions::new().first_pipe_instance(true)
Creates the next server instance before spawning a task for the connected one, so a server instance always exists
Makes the client retry on ERROR_PIPE_BUSY with a short sleep, and treats NotFound as no server
Cites https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/net/windows/named_pipe/struct.NamedPipeServer.html

query: My tokio test for a retry with exponential backoff takes 40 seconds because of the sleeps. How do I make it instant and reliable?
expected_behavior: Recommends #[tokio::test(start_paused = true)] and notes that it needs the test-util feature and a current-thread runtime
Explains auto-advance: with time paused and no other work ready, the clock jumps to the next timer
Uses tokio::time::Instant, not std::time::Instant, for measuring elapsed time under paused time
Prefers sleep with auto-advance over time::advance to force timeouts in order
Cites https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/time/fn.pause.html or https://tokio.rs/tokio/topics/testing
